subject: Resilience mitigation window — proposed SLA carveout and playbook
messages:
From: Srinivas Rao <srinivas@finvault.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@finvault.com>, Legal Ops <contracts@finvault.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: multi-region failover commitments + DR questionnaire

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. To move forward with procurement we need a firm read on Redwood's ability to meet Finvault's regulatory resilience requirements. Specifically:

- RTO and RPO expectations for a primary-region outage that requires failover to a warm standby in another US region.
- Activation lead time (how long between our failover trigger and full traffic shift).
- Any carveouts or exceptions you require (scheduled maintenance, major cloud provider incidents, third-party service failures).

I've attached our DR questionnaire (Finvault_DR_questionnaire_v2.pdf) — please return a completed copy and flag any items where you need contractual exceptions. Legal has asked us to capture proposed handling in a written playbook and a one-page SLA addendum.

Can you respond with a proposed playbook and exception list by EOD Monday? We need internal sign-off the week of Dec 13 to keep the Q4 timeline.

Appreciate it —
Srinivas
Head of Infrastructure, Finvault

---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: multi-region failover commitments + DR questionnaire

Folks — forwarding Finvault's ask. High-level: they want RTO/RPO and an SLA addendum with exceptions called out. Timeline: draft to Srinivas by Monday EOD.

Quick thoughts: I don't want to promise full instantaneous failover cross-region for all customers. Our standard is: hosted customers get warm-standby activation within a stated window depending on reserved capacity. For prospective enterprise customers we can negotiate a narrower activation lead time if they purchase Dedicated reserved capacity or agree to an elevated support tier.

Requesting help:
- Marissa: can you sketch a pragmatic playbook (steps, owner, expected timelines) we can ship Monday? Keep it operational — activation triggers, partial traffic routing, monitoring thresholds.
- Kimberly: Legal will need an exception template for cloud-provider-origin incidents and a concise liability line.
- Neha/Naomi: tech constraints — what's realistic for RPO with cross-region KV/replication? We should surface any data-loss windows.

I'll draft the outward message once we have inputs.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Customer Success (acting)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 14:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: multi-region failover commitments + DR questionnaire

Vivek / team — draft playbook bullets below (operationally focused) that I think we can stand behind for hosted customers (Finvault is evaluating Hosted + Dedicated options):

1) Incident detection & trigger
   - Primary region detected outage via multi-sensor alerts (latency, API errors, region health)
   - Customer may also manually request failover via support portal (customer-triggered).

2) Failover type
   - Warm standby (recommended): pre-provisioned resources in secondary region with model artifacts, partial KV warm cache.

3) Activation lead times (proposed)
   - Partial traffic routing (health checks satisfied): within 30 minutes of trigger.
   - Full traffic shift (scaled to baseline throughput): within 2 hours of trigger.

4) RPO / data loss window
   - For model state and request logs: up to 5 minutes RPO in cross-region warm-standby unless customer opts into synchronous replication (Dedicated customers only).

5) Exceptions / carveouts
   - Major cloud provider-wide outages (where we cannot provision capacity): request temporary carveout and reasonable effort commitment.
   - Scheduled maintenance with 48hr notice (not counted as SLA outage).

6) Post-failover validation & rollback
   - Post-migration smoke-tests, performance KPIs monitored for 24 hours. Rollback only on customer agreement or if performance degradation persists.

I kept the activation windows conservative so we don't over-promise. If Finvault wants tighter SLAs we should push Dedicated + synchronous replication and a higher support tier which I'll price separately. I'll convert this into a one-page playbook and attach.

-Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager

Attachment: redwood-proposed-failover-playbook_v1.docx (docx)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: multi-region failover commitments + DR questionnaire

Thanks — these look good operationally. A few legal flags to include in the customer-facing SLA addendum:

- Liability cap: limit related to failover performance to the value of fees paid in the previous 3 months (standard).
- Carveouts: explicitly enumerate "force majeure" and the subset for cloud provider capacity / networking events where we will use commercially reasonable efforts but cannot guarantee activation windows.
- Customer obligations: customer must follow the documented playbook and provide an authorized failover request channel; if customer initiates an out-of-band failover, we will respond per playbook but cannot guarantee rollback timing.
- Measurement: define the metric used for RTO (time from official failover trigger logged in support portal to 95% of baseline requests responding in secondary region).

If we agree, I can draft the short SLA paragraphs. Also flagging regulatory point: Finvault may require audit evidence (post-mortem within 10 business days) — we should commit to that for enterprise deals.

-Kim
Head of Contracting & Compliance
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Srinivas Rao <srinivas@finvault.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@finvault.com>, Legal Ops <contracts@finvault.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region failover commitments + DR questionnaire

Srinivas — thanks for the questionnaire and patience. Attached is a one-page operational playbook and a short SLA addendum draft. Highlights / proposed carveouts below so you have the summary up front: 

- Activation windows (hosted): partial traffic within 30 minutes; full traffic scaled to baseline within 2 hours.
- RPO (hosted warm-standby): up to 5 minutes for request logs/model state; for <1 minute RPO require synchronous replication on Dedicated.
- Exceptions: major cloud provider outages, network-level partitioning, and scheduled maintenance with 48-hour notice are carved out; in those cases Redwood will provide best-effort activation and transparent incident reports.
- Measurement: RTO measured from the timestamp of the official failover trigger recorded in the support portal to restored service at 95% baseline throughput.
- Post-incident deliverables: incident timeline and remediation steps delivered within 10 business days; we can provide extended evidence under NDA on request.

If Finvault needs a guaranteed <30-minute full-traffic SLA or synchronous cross-region replication we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity plus synchronous replication and a premium support tier; we can provide pricing for that option.

Please review the attached playbook and SLA paragraphs. If acceptable, Legal can mark up the addendum and we can route to DocuSign (I included a placeholder link in the attachments).

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
